title: Polar animal cards
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Living things and their habitats (Frozen Kingdom)
source: Seeded from science/y6 lessons 14, 17 (Polar animal cards (portal worksheet))
intro: To understand how energy passes through polar food chains

questions.q: Write a chain with: polar bear, phytoplankton, ringed seal, Arctic cod, zooplankton.
questions.a: phytoplankton → zooplankton → Arctic cod → ringed seal → polar bear
questions.model: Start with the producer: phytoplankton. Then who eats it? Zooplankton. Then Arctic cod, then ringed seal, then the apex predator: polar bear.

questions.q: Name the apex predator in that chain.
Is a penguin a predator, prey or both?
questions.a: Both: it eats krill and is eaten by leopard seals.

questions.q: Using the key: feathers, can fly. Which animal?
questions.model: Question 1: feathers? Yes, go to 2. Question 2: can it fly? Yes. So it is the snowy owl.

questions.q: Write a question that splits: krill, seal.
questions.a: For example: Does it have a backbone? (seal yes, krill no).

questions.q: Why is 'Is it big?' a poor question?
questions.a: It is an opinion; people would disagree.

questions.q: Core: Use the polar animal cards to build two Antarctic food chains and label each living thing.
questions.a: For example: phytoplankton → krill → crabeater seal → orca; phytoplankton → krill → Adelie penguin → leopard seal.
questions.model: Teacher builds the first: phytoplankton → krill → blue whale. Label: producer, prey, predator.

questions.q: Extend: Explain what would happen to penguins and whales if krill were overfished.
questions.a: They would have less food, so their numbers could fall.

questions.q: Stretch: Join your chains into a food web. Why is a web more realistic?
questions.a: Most animals eat more than one thing, so chains link together.

questions.q: Core: Build a branching key for six household objects or six polar animals (portal cards).
questions.a: Accept any key where each question is observable and every item ends at its own name.
questions.model: Teacher writes the first question for the polar cards: 'Does it have a backbone?' (krill goes one way, the rest the other).

questions.q: Extend: Swap keys with a family member. Did their test reach the right name each time?
Stretch: Improve one question in your key so it is clearer. Explain the change.
questions.a: For example: changed 'Is it large?' to 'Is it longer than 1 m?'

questions.q: Big question: why is tiny krill so important in the Antarctic?
questions.a: So many animals eat krill that, without it, the whole food chain would struggle.

questions.q: Each question in a key should have...
questions.a: A) a yes or no answer

questions.q: Big question: how could you identify an animal you have never seen before?
questions.a: Use a branching key: answer yes/no questions about its features.
